title: Resolving and resetting the charge environment of single T-centers in silicon p-i-n waveguides
authors: Chaoshen Zhang, Hanbin Song, Lukasz Komza, Aaron M. Day, Enrique Garcia, Donald Witt, Mihir K. Bhaskar, Alp Sipahigil, Evelyn L. Hu
abstract: The silicon T-center is a telecom-band spin-photon interface in a manufacturable photonics platform. In nanophotonic devices, however, its optical linewidth is broadened by a fluctuating charge environment, limiting photon indistinguishability for quantum networking. Here, we address this challenge through characterization and suppression of the local charge-noise of single T-centers in lateral p-i-n waveguides, demonstrating an unheralded method of T-center optical linewidth narrowing. Above-band illumination resets the charge environment, neutralizing the local field and suppressing spectral diffusion. Across 46 emitters this reset narrows the median linewidth 3.5-fold to 0.57(11) GHz, and an optimized emitter reaches 128(22) MHz, the narrowest unheralded linewidth reported for an integrated T-center. The narrowed transition supports coherent optical Rabi oscillations with a coherence time of 20(2) ns. Finally, we perform Stark-shift tuning using the p-i-n junction, and read out the local electric field and the charge-noise width at 15 mK. An analytical model of proximal surfaces, bulk, and junction field effects provides good agreement with our findings. Our multi-pronged characterization of the nanophotonic-integrated T-center charge environment enables future device optimization toward scalable quantum interconnects.
summary: The research tackles charge noise broadening in silicon T-centers, a major hurdle for quantum networking. By implementing an above-band optical pulse sequence, the authors successfully reset the local charge environment, dramatically narrowing the spectral linewidth. This demonstrates a robust, scalable method to create high-quality quantum emitters for integrated photonic circuits.
main_problem: The optical linewidth of single T-centers in silicon waveguides is broadened by fluctuating charge environments, which severely limits their use for high-fidelity quantum networking.
main_result: Above-band illumination provides an unheralded method to reset the local charge environment, narrowing the median linewidth by up to 3.5 times and achieving a narrowest reported linewidth of 128 MHz.
method: The authors characterized the charge environment using pulsed photoluminescence excitation (PLE) measurements combined with electrical biasing and optical resetting techniques.
model_or_system: The system involves single T-centers embedded in lateral p-i-n waveguides on silicon. The analysis models the measured spectral lineshape by decomposing the effective field into a deterministic external field ($E_{ext}$) and Gaussian charge noise ($\sigma_E$).
key_observables: Optical linewidth (FWHM), Rabi oscillation coherence time, local electric field shift (Stark effect), and charge-noise width ($\sigma_E$).
important_parameters: Base temperature of 15 mK; initial linewidths in the GHz range; final narrowest linewidth of 128 MHz.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the measured lineshape can be modeled by averaging a Lorentzian over the charge noise distribution, and that the T-center transition frequency follows a quadratic Stark map.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate device schematics, pulse sequences (PLE/AB-PLE), voltage-resolved PLE spectrograms showing linewidth narrowing upon AB reset, and time-resolved measurements tracking charge environment recovery dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem (charge noise limiting indistinguishability) to presenting the novel measurement technique (AB-PLE resetting), quantifying the improvement across many emitters, and finally validating the underlying physics using Stark shift tuning and analytical modeling of the local field.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a critical bottleneck in solid-state quantum photonics by providing an active method to suppress spectral diffusion noise, which is crucial for scaling up quantum interconnects based on spin-photon interfaces.
